summary.intent: Run a CodeRabbit CLI review on the phase 43 (`feat/fuse-write-durability`) branch, cross-check the 8 existing critical findings (CR-01–CR-08) against current code, fix any still-live bugs, apply minor cleanups, reconcile planning docs, and commit everything.
summary.outcome: All 8 criticals verified: 6 were already fixed, CR-03 (TEE-wrapped key written into user-key journal field) was fixed in both the child-key sites and extended to all 6 sibling IPNS-key wrap sites, and CR-04 was resolved by reordering mutations to occur after the journal fsync commit. Three additional CodeRabbit cleanups (journal-dir fallback warn, `to_lowercase`, `wrap_key` path normalization) and doc reconciliation were applied; all 40 fuse unit tests passed and both crates compiled clean, but the commit failed repeatedly due to a wedged 1Password SSH signer.

repo: Phase planning lives in `.planning/phases/<N>-<slug>/` with a `<N>-REVIEW.md` (bug/security review artifact) and `<N>-NN-SUMMARY.md` files; phase numbering is tracked in a separate planning index.

FUSE write durability spans two parallel implementations: fuser (macOS/Linux) in `crates/fuse/src/` and WinFsp (Windows) in `crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/`; they must be kept structurally symmetric.
IPNS key hierarchy has two distinct wrapping schemes — TEE-wrapped (`encrypted_ipns_for_tee`) for live publish requests and user-ECIES-wrapped for journal replay; conflating them bricks replay.
The journal commit must be the serialization point: in-memory mutations (inode.kind, pending_content, queue_publish) must happen *after* `journal.put` succeeds, not before.
Windows winfsp deps are Windows-only; the winfsp feature path cannot be compiled locally on macOS — CI runs `cargo check --features winfsp` as the coverage gate.
Commits are signed via 1Password SSH agent; the signer can wedge after a failed attempt and requires a full restart of the 1Password desktop app to recover.
`cipherbox-fuse` has 40 unit tests covering journal replay and park behavior.

code.finding: CR-03 root site: error fallback used `encrypted_ipns_for_tee.clone().unwrap_or_default()` instead of `String::new()`, silently journaling a TEE-wrapped key into the user-key field, breaking replay. Fixed to warn + empty string.

CR-03 Windows mirror: same TEE-key fallback in child-key journal wrap. Also contained `cipherbox_crypto::wrap_key` calls (lines 148, 152, 886) instead of `cipherbox_crypto::ecies::wrap_key` used elsewhere — cosmetic but a latent compile risk if re-exported path ever diverges.
Parent IPNS key wrap failure silently swallowed via `.ok()`, journaling empty string with no log — same silent-degradation class as CR-03. Hardened to warn-on-failure.

CR-04: `inode.kind`, `pending_content`, and `queue_publish(parent)` were all mutated before `journal.put`, so a journal fsync failure left in-memory state dirty and the debounced publisher could emit metadata for a write the OS was told failed. Fixed by deferring all three mutations to after the journal commit.
Case-sensitive `"not found"` string match; should use `.to_lowercase()` to handle OS-variant casing.

workflow: CodeRabbit CLI can be scoped to a branch's merge-base diff (rather than HEAD) to review only phase-specific changes.
Spawning parallel read-only verification agents per finding is an effective pattern for cross-checking documented review criticals against current code.
Exit code 0 from a piped shell command (e.g. `| tail`) does not mean git succeeded; always verify `git log` after a background commit.
Commit message accuracy matters for design decisions: 'rolls back' vs 'defers mutations' describe different implementations and should match what was actually built.

The `/simplify` skill (quality/reuse cleanups) is distinct from `/code-review` and CodeRabbit (bug/security hunting) and leaves no dedicated artifact — absence of a simplify commit is the only evidence it wasn't run.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged twice with 'failed to fill whole buffer' after an initial failure, requiring a full desktop app restart before the commit could land.
Exit code 0 from the background `git commit | tail` command masked the actual git failure, requiring a separate `git log` verification step to detect the failed commit.
Windows WinFsp path cannot be compile-checked locally on macOS, requiring manual inspection of the reordered region for correctness and reliance on CI.
open_items: CR-04 on the Windows WinFsp path: `Cleanup` returns VOID so it cannot signal failure to the OS — inode rollback was deliberately waived with a code comment; the narrow phantom-publish risk remains accepted.
/simplify pass on the phase-43 diff has never been run and was deferred — CodeRabbit/code-review hunts bugs, /simplify does reuse/efficiency/altitude cleanups.
WR-01 through WR-09 warning-level items from `43-REVIEW.md` were not addressed in this session (only the 8 CR-level criticals were verified and fixed).
Commit was still retrying at end of transcript — final success not confirmed in the session log.
